subtitulo: Five questions about the last minute and the pocket card
introPt: The last morning, four counters, and a goodbye with a season inside it.
cenario: A bakery, a reception desk, and a doorway on the way out.

dialogo.es: いろいろ、ありがとうございました。旅で一番のパンでした。
dialogo.pt: Thank you for everything. That was the best bread of the trip.
dialogo.tts: いろいろ、ありがとうございました。旅で一番のパンでした。

dialogo.es: あら、嬉しい。またぜひ来てくださいね。
dialogo.pt: Oh, how kind. Do come again, won't you.
dialogo.tts: あら、嬉しい。またぜひ来てくださいね。

dialogo.es: 来年の春に。約束します。
dialogo.pt: Next year, in spring. That's a promise.
dialogo.tts: 来年の春に。約束します。

dialogo.es: いえいえ、お上手ですよ！お気をつけて。
dialogo.pt: Not at all, you're very good! Take care on your way.
dialogo.tts: いえいえ、お上手ですよ！お気をつけて。

perguntas.pergunta: The goodbye has three clauses. Which one do visitors leave out?
perguntas.explica: Without the middle clause it is ordinary politeness. Naming the bread is what proves you noticed.

perguntas.pergunta: Mata zehi kite kudasai ne. Best answer?
opcoes: A season and a promise — rainen no haru ni, yakusoku shimasu
An exact date in your diary
A polite smile and nothing else
perguntas.explica: Nobody is booking anything. The loose commitment is the expected shape, and it is what gets remembered.

perguntas.pergunta: Which sentence from the whole course has to be automatic?
perguntas.explica: It is what keeps every other sentence usable when the answer comes back at full speed.

perguntas.pergunta: Someone tells you o-jouzu desu yo. What do you do?
opcoes: Explain how bad your Japanese really is
Take it, and hand a warm line straight back
Switch to English to make it easier
perguntas.explica: Arguing with a compliment costs you the moment. Arigatou, sochira mo o-genki de finishes it properly.

perguntas.pergunta: Mata kimasu, mata ne, mata itsuka. What do they have in common?
opcoes: They all build the next meeting into the word
They are all used only at counters
perguntas.explica: The everyday goodbyes here are open-ended by design; sayounara, the final one, has all but left casual use.
